**Biological Narrative**

The differential metabolite profile is dominated by the **Arachidonic Acid Metabolism** pathway (KEGG map00590), with near-identical enrichment across a cluster of NSAID/analgesic action pathways that overlay this same network. Six of the seven detected compounds are canonical eicosanoids, and all of them are downstream of arachidonic acid, placing this central membrane phospholipid at the head of the affected metabolic cascade.

**Key drivers.** Arachidonic acid (C00219) is the primary upstream precursor driving the entire observed eicosanoid storm. Within the 5-lipoxygenase branch, 5-HETE (C04805) and Leukotriene A4 (C00909) confirm activation of the leukotriene axis, while in the cyclooxygenase/cytochrome-P450 branch, 15-HETE (C04742), 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717), and 11,12,15-THETA (C14782) indicate parallel lipoxygenase and cyclopentenone-prostaglandin outputs. The presence of 11,12,15-THETA suggests a recently described triple lipoxygenation product of arachidonic acid, expanding the pathway footprint beyond the classic HETEs.

**Directional evidence.** KEGG reaction graph analysis confirms arachidonic acid → leukotriene A4 connectivity (2 hops, bidirectional), establishing a clear precursor–product relationship that anchors the narrative. Arachidonic acid is therefore the upstream driver, with its downstream metabolites amplifying the signal as the operational effectors.

**Biological significance.** Arachidonic acid and its eicosanoid daughters are central mediators of inflammation, pain, fever, and immune cell chemotaxis. Coordinated elevation of leukotrienes and cyclopentenone prostaglandins points to simultaneous activation of innate immune and resolution programs — the latter consistent with the anti-inflammatory 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (a PPARγ ligand). CDP (C00112), the only non-eicosanoid compound, did not enrich for any eicosanoid pathway, suggesting it reflects an independent metabolic perturbation (potentially nucleotide metabolism) that may be mechanistically unrelated to the primary inflammatory signature.
